terms.definition: A chemical reaction that releases energy to its surroundings.
terms.function: Warms its surroundings by giving off heat and sometimes light.
terms.whereItIs: The burning campfire in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Exothermic reactions power fires, engines, warmers, and your body.

terms.definition: The energy an exothermic reaction gives off, usually as heat and light.
terms.function: Warms the surroundings and powers everyday energy.
terms.whereItIs: The radiating waves in the model's energy-out layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Released energy is the visible, useful output of these reactions.

terms.definition: The gap between the reactants' high energy and the products' lower energy.
terms.function: Supplies the energy that exothermic reactions release.
terms.whereItIs: The gap between the two energy bars in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains WHY the reaction has energy to give out.

terms.definition: A packet that releases heat through an exothermic reaction when cracked.
terms.function: A familiar everyday example of an exothermic reaction.
terms.whereItIs: The classic example referenced in the lesson.
terms.whyItMatters: Everyday examples make the abstract idea tangible.
